hints: Start by thinking about what aqueous acid does to an ester, it splits it back into its two parent parts.
Hydrolysis of $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COOCH}_3$ gives propanoic acid, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COOH}$, plus methanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$.
Remember $\text{LiAlH}_4$ reduces the carboxylic acid to a primary alcohol with the same carbon count, but leaves an alcohol unchanged.
walkthrough:
**Hydrolyse the ester with aqueous acid**

Acid hydrolysis breaks the ester bond with water to give a carboxylic acid and an alcohol.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COOCH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COOH} + \text{CH}_3\text{OH}$$

**Check what LiAlH4 does to each product**

$\text{LiAlH}_4$ is a strong reducing agent. It reduces carboxylic acids to primary alcohols, but it does not react with alcohols.

So methanol stays as methanol, while propanoic acid is reduced:
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COOH} + 4[\text{H}] \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Identify Y and Z**

The carbon skeleton is kept during reduction, so the 3-carbon acid becomes a 3-carbon primary alcohol, propan-1-ol.

The final pair is therefore methanol and propan-1-ol:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{OH} \text{ and } \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

options.A: Incorrect. Neither hydrolysis product becomes ethanol here. Methanol is formed from the $\text{OCH}_3$ part and is unchanged by $\text{LiAlH}_4$, and the acid part has three carbons so cannot give the two-carbon $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CHOHCH}_3$ is propan-2-ol, a secondary alcohol. Reduction of a carboxylic acid with $\text{LiAlH}_4$ always gives a primary alcohol, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, not a secondary alcohol.
options.C: Incorrect and a very common trap. Students correctly spot $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$ but then shorten the acid to ethanol. Reduction does not remove a carbon, so $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COOH}$ (3 carbons) must give a 3-carbon alcohol, not 2-carbon $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$.
options.D: Correct. Acid hydrolysis gives $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COOH}$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$. $\text{LiAlH}_4$ leaves $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$ unchanged and reduces $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COOH}$ to the primary alcohol $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ with all three carbons retained.
